name: Leonard Schleifer
sec_insider_companies: REGENERON PHARMACEUTICALS, INC. (REGN) - Bd. Co-Chair, President & CEO
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); SEC insider holdings (2025)
forbes_bio: Leonard Schleifer cofounded drugmaker Regeneron in 1988, and remains CEO of the Tarrytown, New York-based company.
Schleifer took Regeneron public in 1991; he owns 2% of the company's common stock.
Sales of Regeneron's blockbuster drug Eylea, a treatment for macular degeneration, were $4.8 billion in the U.S. in 2024.
Regeneron has developed 12 FDA-approved medicines.
forbes_facts: Schleifer attended Cornell on scholarship and dreamed of a medical career.
The son of a sweater manufacturer, Schleifer grew up in Queens, New York.

name: Lucio Tan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (1996-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Lucio Tan is the founder and chairman of LT Group, which has interests in tobacco, spirits, banking and property development.
In 1982, Tan established Asia Brewery. Now a subsidiary of LT, the brewery was the only one then to compete with the market leader San Miguel.
Tan's grandson and heir apparent Lucio Tan III was appointed president of LT Group and PAL Holdings in 2023.
forbes_facts: Tan studied chemical engineering at Far Eastern University.
PAL Holdings, the parent company of Philippine Airlines, completed its debt restructuring and turned profitable in 2021 after four years of losses.

name: Eddie Zakay
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2011-2021); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
forbes_bio: Brothers Sol and Eddie Zakay are chairman and deputy-chairman of Topland Group, an investment group with a substantial real estate portfolio.
In February 2019, Topland sold the 26 hotels under its Hallmark brand for approximately $325 million (250 million British pounds).
Among its current hotel properties are London's Hilton Brighton Metropole, the luxurious Royal Crescent Hotel in Bath and the Glasgow Hilton.
The Zakay brothers launched Topland in the U.K. in the 1980s. The group also has interests in lending, healthcare and natural resources.

name: Jonathan Tisch
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Jonathan Tisch's late father Bob (d. 2005) started Loews Corporation with his brother Laurence as a New Jersey hotel venture in 1946.
Tisch is co-chairman of Loews alongside his cousin Andrew Tisch; he's also the CEO of Loews' hotel unit.
Loews is active in insurance, drilling rigs, natural gas pipelines and hotels.
His father Bob also bought a 50% stake in the New York Giants for $75 million in 1991.
Jonathan's brother Steve is chairman and executive vice president of the Giants, which FORBES values at $6.3 billion (net of debt).
forbes_facts: He and his wife Lizzie donated more than $2.8 million to the the University of Michigan Museum of Art in May 2019.
The Jonathan M. Tisch College of Civic Life at Tufts University, which promotes youth civic engagement, is named after him.

name: Zhuo Jun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Hurun China (2018-2026); Hurun Self-Made Women (2019-2025)
forbes_bio: Zhuo Jun took over a substantial stake of Shenzhen Kinwong Electronic in 2013 when her husband, Shen Jitang, passed away.
Founded in 1993, the Shanghai-listed company is one of China's largest printed circuit board makers. It announced its plan for a dual listing in Hong Kong in 2025.
Zhuo sits on the board of Kinwong; her younger brother Zhuo Yong serves as vice chairman.
She was a clerk at Heung Yee Kuk, a statutory advisory body representing interests in the New Territories, Hong Kong, for 4 years after high school.
Kinwong is building a printed circuit board manufacturing base in Thailand, its first overseas site, slated to come onstream in 2026.

name: Prem Kumar Arora
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun India (2019)
forbes_bio: Prem Kumar Arora gets the bulk of his wealth from his stake in Indian generics maker Mankind Pharma.
The company was founded by his wife's brothers Ramesh and Rajeev Juneja in 1995.
Mankind Pharma sells generic drugs including antibiotics and treatments for cardiovascular diseases in over two dozen markets worldwide.
The company went public in India in May 2023, raising 43.3 billion rupees ($529 million).

name: Alexander Skorobogatko
name_chinese: 亚历山大·斯科罗博加特科
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Alexander Skorobogatko and partner Alexander Ponomarenko started out with sea ports and banking and then moved into airport construction.
In 2013 the two, with Arkady Rotenberg, a judo partner of President Vladimir Putin, won a tender to develop Sheremetyevo, the state-owned airport.
The partners and Rotenberg also founded TPS Real Estate, which owns more than half of the real estate in Ocean Plaza, Kiev's biggest shopping center.
In 2023 the center was seized by Ukrainian government.
The two Alexanders first set up a small perfume factory in the Ukraine and then founded a bank in Moscow.
forbes_facts: Skorobogatko is a candidate to become a master of sports in judo and sambo.

name: Natacha Nikolajevic
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Natacha Nikolajevic is the widow of Olivier Dassault, an heir to the Dassault aerospace and software fortune.
Olivier Dassault's grandfather founded Dassault Aviation, a French aerospace company that started out making propellers in World War I.
Nikolajevic's husband Olivier, a prominent French politician who served as a representative in France's National Assembly, died in a helicopter crash in 2021.
The Dassault family also own the country's daily newspaper Le Figaro, several vineyards and a private aeronautic company.
forbes_facts: She met her late billionaire husband Olivier during an auction where they competed for the same item.

name: Pan Weiming
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2016-2020); Hurun Global (2014-2019); Hurun China (2010-2019)
forbes_bio: Pan Weiming chairs the Fullsun Group, whose main businesses are construction and property development.
Pan quit his job of a magistrate in 1993 in Conghua in Guangdong and started his first property company with his brother.

name: Edward Lampert
sec_insider_companies: LANDS' END, INC. (LE) - TenPercentOwner; Seritage Growth Properties (SRG) - TenPercentOwner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2004-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: After a stint at Goldman Sachs' risk arbitrage department, Edward Lampert founded hedge fund ESL Investments in 1988, betting on undervalued stocks.
He took over as CEO of struggling retail giant Sears Holdings (Sears, Kmart, Kenmore) in 2013 with hopes of a turnaround, but failed miserably.
Lampert's ESL Investments promised Sears nearly $1 billion in loans in the first 10 months of 2017.
In October 2018, Sears Holdings filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and announced that it would close 142 Sears and Kmart stores.
In January 2019 Lampert won an auction to keep the company, with a reported bid of more than $5 billion.
forbes_facts: Lampert survived a kidnapping in 2003; his captors released him after two days.
A graduate of Yale University, he was a part of the secret society Skull and Bones, whose alumni include former presidents George H.W. Bush and George W. Bush.
